newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Radio pirate stirs panic in Belgian airspace.
newsitem.headline: Radio pirate stirs panic in Belgian airspace.

text.p: A radio pirate posing as an air traffic controller has been broadcasting false instructions to pilots to disrupt their landings and cause accidents, air traffic authorities said on Wednesday.
But the Brussels airport authority insisted there was no actual danger.
A spokesman for the air traffic authorities told BRTN radio that the unknown man has been misleading pilots since October by breaking into the normal air traffic radio frequencies.

"He tells them how to land, the normal messages -- a bit higher, a bit lower, a bit to the left, right, that kind of instructions," he said. "He can only have bad intentions...this could lead to accidents."
The man, who operates mainly from eastern Belgium, is familiar with the specialised air traffic vocabulary, he said.
"He knows so much about it that we believe he was involved (in air transport)...he is a major threat to air transport," he said.
Mobile teams have so far failed to catch the radio pirate who is using a mobile transmitter.
Brussels airport authority chairman Eric Kirsch told BRTN that pilots flying to the capital's airport were given strict security instructions.

"When a controller gives instructions to the pilot, the pilot has to repeat them so that the controller can check that the pilot has well understood them...This is why I can say...there is no danger," Kirsch said. -- Bert Lauwers, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6815, Fax +32 2 230 7710
